September, 2024
Neutral Citation No. 2024:Mphc-Gwl:15716

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Gwalior
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Rajendra Kumar Vani

On The 12 th Of September, 2024
 Criminal Appeal No. 7697 of 2024
 Raman Bhargarv
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Ajay Bhargava - Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri Bhanu Pratap Singh Chauhan - Public Prosecutor for the State.
 Order

The appellant has filed this first criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 being aggrieved by order dated 29.06.2024 passed by the Special Judge (Atrocities) Act, Datia (M.P.) whereby bail application u/S 439 of Cr.P.C. of appellant has been rejected.

Sections 3(1)(w)(ii) and 3(2)(va) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and Sections 25/27 of the Arms Act.

sentences.text: 4.Not Learned falsely been implicated in the matter.
He is in custody since 02.06.2024.

It is NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-GWL:15716 2 CRA-7697-2024 further submitted that co-accused Bharat Ahirwar and Bharat Parihar have been granted bail by the Coordinate Bench of this Court vide order dated 27.06.2024 passed in Criminal Appeal No.7011 of 2024 and the case of present appellant is identical to that of aforesaid co-accused.
The trial is likely to take long time to conclude.
The appellant is ready and willing to abide by any conditions which may be imposed by the Court.
On these grounds, he prays that the impugned order be set aside and appellant may be extended the benefit of bail.

sentences.text: Per contra , learned counsel for the State opposes the appeal and prays for its rejection. .

6. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
7.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and facts and circumstances of the case,
coupled with the fact that case of the applicant is akin to that of aforesaid co-accused who have been released on bail, while setting aside the order dated 29.06.2024 passed by the Trial Court, this Court is inclined to release the appellant on bail.

Thus, without commenting on the merits of the case, the appeal is allowed but with certain stringent conditions and it is directed that the appellant be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rs. One Lac Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court/Committal Court.
Certified copy as per rules.

(RAJENDRA KUMAR VANI) JUDGE ms/-
